A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching the retained Appendices A–H.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original COMPAS analysis, including computed feasible regions and fair versus unconstrained accuracies of 0.677 and 0.681.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendices I–J report original FICO, COMPAS, and ACS Income analyses, synthetic perturbation experiments, and calibration-subsampling results.

M1.justification: The boundary-tracing algorithm, randomized selection-rule construction, and loss/separation objectives remain unchanged. The new experiments apply this method; Algorithm 2 only corrects an argmax dummy index.

E1.justification: v2 adds FICO creditworthiness and California ACS Income prediction to the original COMPAS coverage. COMPAS changes from Caucasian versus all non-Caucasian defendants to Caucasian versus African-American defendants. Appendix J additionally evaluates perturbed score inputs.

E2.justification: The new ACS experiment introduces a raw logistic-regression classifier thresholded at 0.5 as a comparator, beyond v1's unconstrained optimum on the COMPAS calibrated-score model. COMPAS retains its Bayes comparison, and FICO extends that comparison type; newly cited competing fairness algorithms are not evaluated.

E3.justification: COMPAS changes from a score-stratified 20% calibration/80% distribution-estimation split to an explicitly unsplit aggregate analysis. ACS introduces an 80/20 train/test design, five-fold out-of-fold calibration, 100 group-specific bins, test-score weight estimation without test labels, and evaluation of randomized decisions in expectation. Appendix J adds perturbation and calibration-subsampling protocols.

E4.justification: New Appendix J tests sensitivity to imperfect calibration through synthetic score perturbations and reduced ACS calibration samples. Figures 6–7 examine resulting PPV/FOR violations and accuracy stability; v1 contains no corresponding robustness analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty reporting. v2 adds 100 ACS splits, 95% percentile-bootstrap intervals using 10,000 resamples, and distributional boxplots. Robustness experiments report 100 perturbations per error level and 20 calibration subsamples per split where applicable.

E6.justification: Under changed COMPAS population and settings, fair/unconstrained accuracies become 0.6563/0.6629 instead of 0.677/0.681; the separation-minimizing classifier now differs from the accuracy optimum, attaining 0.6526. These are replaced results, not comparable performance declines. New FICO and ACS fair/unconstrained accuracies are 0.8676/0.8819 and 0.8167/0.8190, alongside parity-gap and robustness findings.

T1.justification: Appendix J adds a derivation proving that each group-wise PPV/FOR gap is at most twice the maximum calibration error. v2 also corrects Definition 3.2 to optimize over the fixed-selection-rate set Cµ and changes Equation (9) from an equivalence to a necessary implication. The earlier principal theorems and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the original geometric characterization and exact-optimality contributions remain. The new conclusion adds a practical robustness claim concerning approximate calibration and small empirical predictive-parity violations.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability qualifications: COMPAS is explicitly illustrative under assumed group calibration, and ACS may violate exact predictive parity on held-out data. The conclusion discusses approximate calibration, the practical rationale for finite score bins, and increasingly restrictive feasibility with more protected groups.

D1.justification: Appendix I adds score-construction formulas, COMPAS filtering instructions, data-source identifiers, and ACS feature processing, logistic-regression training, calibration, and evaluation details. Appendix J specifies perturbations and subsampling. An introductory footnote supplies a future code-release location, without establishing that code is already available.

R1.justification: v2 adds Celis, Delaney, and Zeng to distinguish approximate or positive-decision-only fairness from exact sufficiency, plus references on calibration, multicalibration, discretization, and ACS. The central positioning relative to Canetti and Baumann remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing exposition and section organization are retained. Section 7 becomes three experimental subsections, and v2 adds a conclusion, impact statement, and explanatory footnotes clarifying predictive parity and star-convexity, alongside localized wording edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds the FICO plot and three-panel ACS and robustness displays in Figures 5–7, and redraws the revised COMPAS analysis as Figure 4. Figure 2 changes from vertically stacked to side-by-side panels with revised colors, markers, and legend; Figure 1 is resized.

improvement.justification: v1 supports practical applicability mainly through one COMPAS illustration despite relying on group calibration. v2 substantially addresses this gap with a calibration-error guarantee, targeted robustness experiments, and repeated held-out ACS evaluation with confidence intervals. It also corrects two formal statements and documents implementation substantially better. COMPAS remains an illustrative constructed-score analysis with changed settings, but the additional evidence materially strengthens the unchanged method's reliability and practical relevance.
